You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 01 — Keel
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** Pre-dawn Keel pump hall. Alex presses his scarred palm to a trembling housing while a salvaged bracket holds a cracked pipe. Workers wait with narrow water containers. A white-and-amber control node watches.
SUPERVISOR: That isn't approved.
**Panel 2.** Alex tightens the bracket. The gauge shifts from red toward amber, though the warning remains.
ALEX: It's holding.
SFX: THRUMM—THRUMM
**Panel 3.** The supervisor reaches for the node.
ALEX: Then don't approve it. Just notice it works.
**Panel 4.** The node stamps the repair:
**UNAUTHORIZED REPAIR — REVIEW REQUIRED**
The supervisor forces the warning shut.
SFX: KTHUNK
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** End-of-shift checkpoint. Alex scans his wristband. The same network reads him.
**ALEX PHANTUM — AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN**
**PARENTAL HOUSEHOLD LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE**
**GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**  
**DEBT BALANCE: 418,607 CREDITS**  
**EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS**
A guard looks at the screen, then at Alex.
GUARD: Happy birthday, Phantum.
**Panel 2.** The display adds:
**PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS**  
**TRAVEL STATUS: RESTRICTED**
Behind Alex, workers go quiet.
**Panel 3.** Alex stares at **WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED**, turning Adrian's worn casino chip in his pocket. A small archived line appears beneath the balance:
**ORIGIN: ADRIAN PHANTUM — PARTS LOAN / GAMBLING COLLATERAL**
**Panel 4.** Alex walks through the gate. The debt remains suspended behind him like a sign nobody can take down.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
SFX: BEEP—CLACK
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** Evening at Inez Quispe's pharmacy. A prescription packet and travel token sit on the counter. Ada checks the label and ties a canvas pouch shut.
INEZ: Thirty credits for your grandmother. Forty-two for the token.
ALEX: I have fifty-two.
INEZ: Then one gets paid today.
**Panel 2.** Inez opens her blue-cloth ledger.
INEZ: I front the medicine. You return thirty by next shift. The token waits.
Alex takes the medicine pouch, leaving the token on the counter.
**Panel 3.** Alex reaches for the token anyway. Ada catches his wrist.
ADA: Halyard?
ALEX: Somewhere that isn't here.
ADA: You know a direction.
ALEX: I know enough.
**Panel 4.** Ada pushes the token across to him.
ADA: I'm coming. You don't know the route.
Inez writes:
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS**
**FIRST PAYMENT — NEXT SHIFT**
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** Next evening. Inez's pharmacy is half-shuttered. Alex stands empty-handed at the counter. Ada waits outside.
INEZ: You missed the date.
ALEX: Site 6 took the shift.
INEZ: The shift took your wages. You still missed the date.
**Panel 2.** Alex places his wristband beside the ledger.
**MEDICINE ADVANCE — 30 CREDITS — UNPAID**
ALEX: I'm not asking you to erase it.
INEZ: Good. I need the money.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother's apartment. Alex hands her the medicine. Her worn cloth sits beside the prescription.
GRANDMOTHER: By the blue cup. I can find the blue cup.
**Panel 4.** Grandmother hands Alex Adrian's book.
GRANDMOTHER: Put it where it fits.
Alex places it on a shelf. A hidden catch depresses.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** Behind the bookcase: Adrian's cramped workshop. Analog gauges, folded water plans, an old paper survey marked with route ticks and a covered machine.
**Panel 2.** Alex finds Adrian's looping equation beside a water-routing diagram. The casino chip bears the same loop, but no slot accepts it.
ALEX: Same hand. Different damage.
GRANDMOTHER: He was working. He had already lost everything.
**Panel 3.** Grandmother's eyes sharpen as she points to the water plans.
GRANDMOTHER: He kept saying the lower line was thirsty. I told him to stop betting on being right.
**Panel 4.** Alex lifts a brass key labeled:
**B11 / DEPLOYMENT**
ALEX: This is the part he left on purpose.
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the key into the compact machine.
SFX: TIK—TIK—WHIRR
**Panel 2.** B11 unfolds onto the workbench: mismatched brass and ceramic, repaired joints, amber eyes and a faded rust-red scarf.
B11: Well. That took longer than expected.
ALEX: You were asleep.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** B11 studies Alex's wristband.
B11: You are Adrian's son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** A second compartment opens beneath B11's chest plate. Beside a dormant recording cartridge rests a dark engraved band marked **ADRIAN**.
B11: I have a route. I also have a question.
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Adrian's interrupted recording appears above the bench. Alex and B11 watch.
ADRIAN: If B11 is awake, the old line may still be carrying water.
**Panel 2.** The recording shows an official Keel allocation beside a physical pipe drawing.
ADRIAN: The record says one thing. The pipe may say another.
**Panel 3.** A paper map descends beneath the sealed mine. A marked chamber is labeled:
**LEGACY NODE — LIVE ROUTING**
ADRIAN: Bring the physical reading back. Don't trust my conclusion.
**Panel 4.** The workshop node sends an amber pulse upward.
SFX: PIP—PIP—PIP
B11: Someone noticed.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** Oasis control room. Mera stands beside a white-and-amber node. The display shows:
**LEGACY NODE SIGNAL — KEEL**
**AVAILABLE ROUTES: SEALED / ASSIGNED / UNMONITORED**
**Panel 2.** Mera selects **TRACK**.
MERA: Site 6. Put the signal where a mechanic can reach it.
**Panel 3.** The node highlights Alex's record. Mera's hand stops short of the assignment field.
**EXECUTIVE SCOPE: ROUTING ONLY**
**Panel 4.** Alex's wristband lights in the workshop:
**SHIFT REASSIGNED: EXTRACTION SITE 6 — 02:14**  
**TRAVEL CLEARANCE: CONDITIONAL**
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada unfolds her hand-marked map beneath a lamp. Ticks mark every third junction.
ADA: Third junction. Then the old works.
ALEX: You know this route?
ADA: I know what people stop repairing.
**Panel 2.** Alex checks his wristband. A small status line reads:
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY: ACTIVE**
**Panel 3.** Site 6 gate. Foreman-7 rolls into view. B11 is folded inside Alex's tool bag.
FOREMAN-7: Companion clearance denied.
Ada holds up Alex's assignment.
ADA: He is assigned repair labor. The bag is equipment.
**Panel 4.** The gate admits Alex. B11 remains hidden inside the bag.
SFX: K-CHUNK
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A hauling frame has collapsed across Tomas. Dust pours from a damaged ventilation line. A yellow boundary divides the work zones.
TOMAS: That's not regulation.
**Panel 2.** Alex kneels at the boundary. His wristband flashes:
**ASSIGNED ZONE: HOLD POSITION**
Ada grips his strap.
ADA: Alex.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps over the line.
SFX: BEEP—BEEP
**Panel 4.** His wristband displays:
**LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR**
ALEX: That is today's pay.
ADA: I know.
---
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame with a jack. Tomas's leg is trapped but not crushed.
ALEX: Can you breathe?
TOMAS: Enough to complain.
**Panel 2.** B11 opens his torso compartment. Magnetic mine parts lift from it: wedge head, barrel body, four legs and an oversized red magnet.
SFX: TAK—TAK—TAK
**Panel 3.** TJ stands crooked but recognizably dog-shaped. Its head tilts.
B11: TJ. Site scout.
TJ: KRRIP.
**Panel 4.** TJ detaches its head and sends it through a gap toward a jammed release.
TOMAS: That dog yours?
B11: Recently.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ finds the jammed release.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 2.** Alex follows the lens light and pulls the release. The frame rises. Tomas crawls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Tomas pulls a long brass key from beneath his shirt.
TOMAS: Your father asked me to keep a door.
ALEX: He ask you to keep him out?
TOMAS: He didn't ask enough.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 rolls into the tunnel. Tomas kicks a maintenance cart across its route.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized shutdown. Remain for protective detention.
TOMAS: Log the shutdown under me. Then go.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas and two miners jam the cart across the tunnel while Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ reach the old door.
TOMAS: Go.
**Panel 2.** Alex fits Tomas's key into the corroded lock. The hinges are clean.
SFX: KLIK—KRAK
**Panel 3.** Hidden chamber: analog gauges, condensation and newer control lines routed through obsolete mine walls.
**Panel 4.** Close on two pipes:
**KEEL RESIDENTIAL** — nearly silent.
**UPLINK INDUSTRIAL** — vibrating.
Alex touches them.
ALEX: The survey says straight.
ADA: The bolts say somebody turned.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** An official display reads:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**
The residential pipe is dry enough to show a mineral ring.
**Panel 2.** Alex follows condensation to a recessed mounting trace. B11 pries loose a rusted cover.
SFX: SKRNNK
**Panel 3.** The compact brass Measure rests inside. Its casing bears a balanced water-drop mark. B11 lifts it carefully.
B11: It has been waiting in the dark longer than I have.
**Panel 4.** Alex connects one arm to the residential pipe and another to the network's data line.
**SENSE**
SFX: HUMMMMM
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** The Measure displays:
**PHYSICAL FLOW: 18%**  
**REPORTED FLOW: 62%**
**Panel 2.** Alex connects the third arm to the industrial line. A blue trace travels through the wall toward a maintained bypass.
**COMPARE — TRACE**
**Panel 3.** The node flashes cold white. The bypass-side door seals.
SFX: K-CHUNK—K-CHUNK
**Panel 4.** A narrow maintenance channel remains open. Beyond it: a marked residential-service hatch and the main conduit.
B11: One way gets you out unseen. One gets you to the homes. The third carries pressure.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** Ada studies the map and reaches the residential-service hatch.
ADA: This hatch meets the conduit wall.
ALEX: And the private channel gets us out unseen.
**Panel 2.** Ada pulls the hatch wheel free. The opening leads to a dry ledge beside the main conduit.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 3.** Alex's wristband offers:
**SEND VERIFIED RECORD TO KEEL**
**CONSEQUENCE: ROUTE EXPOSURE / ACCESS CLOSURE**
Alex looks from the dry ledge to the Measure.
ALEX: If we leave, it stays paper-clean.
He presses **SEND**.
**Panel 4.** Public screens across Keel update:
**REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%**  
**DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%**
Behind them, the private channel slams shut.
SFX: WHUMM—KRAK
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada stand on the ledge beside the main conduit. The residential hatch remains separate from the pipe regulator.
ADA: This only gets us to the wall.
**Panel 2.** Oasis. Mera turns a manual valve labeled:
**CONDUIT SEGMENT — ASCENT PRESSURE**
MERA: Open the segment. Not the homes.
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, pressure shakes the tunnel. A relay carrying worker telemetry tears loose beside Tomas.
FOREMAN-7: Worker-status relay damaged.
TOMAS: Then hold the line.
**Panel 4.** The conduit begins taking pressure. A pale current moves upward beyond the ledge.
SFX: WHUMM—WHUMM
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** The service hatch opens into the main conduit. Alex pulls Ada through. B11 folds against his chest; TJ's magnetic feet lock to the wall.
SFX: SHHHHHRRRAK
**Panel 2.** Water begins filling the lower channel behind them. The conduit trembles under the opened segment valve.
**Panel 3.** Alex checks his wristband:
**SITE 6 WORKER TELEMETRY — INTERRUPTED**
The last image is Tomas's relay light going dark.
**Panel 4 — FULL-PAGE SPLASH.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ climb toward a pale opening as water rises behind them.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ spill from a Halyard storm drain into engineered greenery beside fabrication towers.
ALEX: That was not a route.
B11: It was a route. The destination objected.
**Panel 2.** A registry node scans Alex:
**ALEX PHANTUM — KEEL STATUS — REVIEW PENDING**
**Panel 3.** Ada finds an incomplete packet pushed through the damaged Site 6 channel:
**TOMAS — WORKER TELEMETRY INTERRUPTED**
**STATUS: UNRESOLVED**
ADA: We don't know.
**Panel 4.** A delivery cart passes, marked:
**MORROW & SONS — MARA MORROW — KEEL**
ADA: Mara's still shipping.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** The cart's order sheet is clipped to a crate:
**MORROW & SONS — KEEL**
**CUSTOMER ORDER — PAID**
**PARTS TO BE BUILT — LISTED**
The crate contains replacement filters for the household purifier.
**Panel 2.** Nearby, a fabrication worker places a component in a House kiosk. Her hand remains on it after the machine takes it.
**OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS**
**Panel 3.** The worker tries to retrieve the component. The kiosk locks it behind glass.
WORKER: I made the correction.
KIOSK: HOUSE PROPERTY — DISPOSITION PENDING.
**Panel 4.** B11 watches the cart continue toward Keel.
B11: One customer paid for a thing. One worker got paid for losing hers.
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** Registry hall. Lock approaches, turning a black stylus once.
LOCK: Alex Phantum. Director Cassian Lock.
**Panel 2.** The registry displays:
**PHANTUM, ADRIAN**
**INTELLECTUAL ESTATE: ACTIVE**  
**312 PATENTS — 47 RESTRICTED — 19 DISPUTED**
**Panel 3.** Lock indicates the restricted entries.
LOCK: Those cannot be sold by a claimant. Charter review is required.
ALEX: So it's not money.
LOCK: Not until someone carries the risk.
**Panel 4.** Lock turns the stylus again.
LOCK: I can make it spendable tonight.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lock leads Alex and Ada above Caldera, Vector and Orbital production floors. Screens show materials, testing and distribution moving at industrial speed.
LOCK: This is what scale buys.
**Panel 2.** Alex's registry search reveals a collaborator ledger attached to Adrian's work:
**LINA VEY — MEMBRANE**
**SURI ANIK — BIOFILTER**
**JALEN ORR — NODE LOGIC**
**REN OKAFOR — RECOVERY / HEAT**
**Panel 3.** A worker's contribution enters a House registry. Her name disappears beneath a House ownership line.
ADA: Her hand is still on it.
**Panel 4.** Lock lays down the transfer document.
LOCK: Assign the disputed estate to House administration. Your debt clears tonight. Their reviews stop.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera maintenance floor. Lina works beneath a membrane rig while patrol lights sweep. A cloudy feeder line pulses beside a dry test pipe.
LINA: Keel's line was diverted. This feeder is contaminated. Do not combine the failures.
**Panel 2.** Suri's living biofilter columns flicker weakly behind glass. Lina presses a folded membrane into Alex's hand.
LINA: Take this and the House owns the design by morning.
**Panel 3.** Lock's transfer document appears on Alex's wristband:
**ACCEPT — DEBT CLEARANCE / COLLABORATOR PROTECTION**
**REFUSE — CHARTER REVIEW CONTINUES**
**Panel 4.** Alex looks through the glass at Suri's failing columns.
ALEX: If I sign, who keeps that alive?
LINA: Nobody in the registry.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** Suri kneels beside the biofilter columns. Jalen works at a monitored power node while patrol light passes.
SURI: It needs a steady draw.
JALEN: The monitored line is the only live line.
**Panel 2.** Suri transfers culture into a protected vial. Jalen reroutes power.
SFX: TIK-TIK-TIK
**Panel 3.** A registry entry flashes:
**BIOFILTER CONTRIBUTION: CALDERA HOUSE**  
**CREATOR: UNLISTED**
Suri shields the vial with both hands.
SURI: If they take the name, they take the maintenance.
**Panel 4.** Lina slips the bronze Maker's Seal from her uniform. Alex sees the open-hand medallion.
LINA: Keep the work attached to the people who can keep it alive.
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Jalen opens a service door toward the fabrication bay.
JALEN: Ren's recovery unit is inside. The clean corridor crosses Suri's power line.
ADA: You can get out without it.
JALEN: Then the line dies.
**Panel 2.** Jalen holds the reroute while Alex, Ada, Lina and Suri cross.
JALEN: Eleven seconds. After that, the pattern has my shape.
**Panel 3.** Ren cuts a recovery module from a House fixture. A red heat warning blooms.
SFX: VRRRAK—TINK
REN: This is my unrecorded correction.
**Panel 4.** Ren shoves the module toward Alex, then turns back to the hot bay.
REN: Take the part. I take the heat.
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex stops in the service corridor.
ALEX: No.
He hands the recovery unit to Ada and turns back.
**Panel 2.** Ren braces the overheating fixture while Alex removes a warped heat shield. Suri feeds the living culture through a temporary line.
SFX: HISS—CLANG
**Panel 3.** Jalen breaks the monitored pattern by opening three false maintenance routes. Lina seals the membrane in a dry case.
JALEN: Now.
**Panel 4.** The group reaches a rented maker room above a repair shop. Ren drops the damaged recovery unit on the bench.
SFX: K-CLACK
REN: If it fails, it fails where I can touch it.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lina, Suri, Jalen and Ren connect their components around a test vessel. Alex watches the edges. B11 unfolds; TJ guards the vent.
SFX: KLIK—KLIK—KLIK
**Panel 2.** The unit shudders. Water clouds.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 11%**
**Panel 3.** Suri checks the dead biofilter cycle. Jalen watches a dead signal band.
SURI: The culture never gets its draw.
JALEN: The node sends it.
REN: The heat has nowhere to go.
**Panel 4.** Lina pulls apart a connector.
LINA: They were designed not to meet.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex runs his thumb along the vibrating connector edges.
JALEN: The node is sending.
LINA: The membrane is receiving.
REN: The casing is choking the heat.
**Panel 2.** Alex removes the connector.
ALEX: The edge is wrong.
REN: Metal tells you what it can hold.
**Panel 3.** Ren hands him a thin salvaged sleeve.
REN: It isn't a connector.
ALEX: It can be.
**Panel 4.** Alex fits the sleeve between the edges. The unit steadies. Water clears.
**SIMULATED RECOVERY: 94%**
SFX: HUMMMMM
B11: I expected a longer failure.
ALEX: You can have one later.
---
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** The 94% unit fills most of the room. Three people service it. The casing climbs into the red.
SFX: HISS
**Panel 2.** Ren pulls the heat shield free. Steam blasts across the room.
REN: Industrial flow. Industrial heat. Industrial staff.
**Panel 3.** Suri protects the culture vial as the cycle stutters.
SURI: A family cannot keep this alive.
**Panel 4.** Lina looks at the compact housing on the bench.
LINA: Smaller means less output.
ALEX: Less output than what?
LINA: Less than the House promises. More than Keel gets now.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** House security closes around the maker district. A route projects across the room. Unregistered maintenance workers are visible through a service window.
**Panel 2.** B11 scans the route.
B11: The lowest-risk exit uses six recorded bodies.
ALEX: There are more than six.
B11: The others are not recorded.
**Panel 3.** Alex looks through the window.
ALEX: Then the route is wrong.
**Panel 4.** B11's amber eyes dim.
B11: I counted the record and missed the people. What would you do?
ALEX: Take the long way. Tell them first.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** Ada opens a rusted maintenance hatch absent from the registry. TJ scouts ahead.
ADA: This way is thin.
ALEX: Thin still carries.
**Panel 2.** Inside the room, Lina folds the membrane into a smaller housing. Suri reduces the living draw. Jalen cycles power. Ren redirects waste heat into a warming plate.
**Panel 3.** The compact unit runs:
**HOUSEHOLD CONFIGURATION: 91% RECOVERY**  
**CLEANING REQUIRED**
**REPLACEMENT PARTS REQUIRED**
**Panel 4.** The first replacement cartridge cracks under pressure. Mara Morrow's order packet sits beside it, already marked with a customer request for two spares.
MARA (recorded order): If it needs parts, list the parts.
---

**Panel 1.** Halyard maker room. Alex seals the household unit in a plain crate. Mara's order packet is clipped to the lid:

I'm approaching this like a skeptical high schooler doing a cold read, so I want to be blunt and specific about my reactions. The pump hall opening with Alex fixing something unauthorized is a decent hook, and the birthday debt reveal — inheriting 418,607 credits of debt at 17, spread over 28.7 years — really lands as a strong gut-punch moment.

But then P3 loses me: Ada shows up at the pharmacy with zero introduction, the "Halyard" and travel token business reads like a riddle I can't solve, and it's unclear if he actually takes the token or how Inez's payment setup works. P4-P6 keep piling on unexplained jargon — "Site 6 took the shift," the grandmother's blue cup riddle, the convenient hidden catch in the book, and then B11 the robot with a fun personality but a baffling "ADRIAN" band marking and an unanswered question — it all feels like worldbuilding thrown at me without enough grounding to track what's actually happening.

Now I'm into the recording about "the old line may still be carrying water," which is vague, then Mera at Oasis — unclear who she is or what Oasis even is — reassigning him to Site 6, which reads as helping but is confusing given her executive scope language. Ada somehow gets into a restricted area despite not being assigned, Tomas gets trapped with Alex stepping over a line to forfeit wages in a genuinely clear stakes moment, and then there's a fun detail about a dog assembled from mine parts with a detachable head. Tomas's key scene with the repeated "he didn't ask enough" line lands as the emotional sacrifice beat, the pipe survey reveal is clear-ish, and now I'm looking at the 18% vs 62% water measurement reveal, which seems to be the real payoff about Keel skimming reported water, though the capitalized "Measure" detail is nagging at me.

The escape sequence has three unclear routes, then a cliffhanger with Tomas possibly drowning that doesn't hit hard since I barely know him — I'm left wondering if I actually need issue 2 just to find out his fate. I also notice we never see the Keel residents react to the 18% reveal, so the water wars stakes feel underdeveloped. Moving into issue 2, there's a funny exchange about a route whose "destination objected," then references to Tomas's packet and a "Mara" who's never been introduced, plus a worker kiosk scene that lands the exploitation theme fairly clearly, though a line spelling out the moral feels preachy, and now there's a mention of patents tied to Adrian that raises a new question about his backstory.

Several riddle-like lines pile up — about debt, carrying risk, not combining failures, and ownership of designs — that I have to reread without fully grasping, plus a growing cast of names I likely won't retain. There's a heist sequence with geography I can't quite follow, but the reveal that components were deliberately designed to be incompatible is a neat twist, and Alex's fix with a sleeve feels satisfying even if it's a familiar hero-saves-the-day beat. The story then escalates to something too big for one family, and a recorded-bodies route six moment lands as a decent beat about moral learning, though again a bit over-explained.

The climax itself turns out to be bureaucratic — registry displays, public licenses, a seal mismatch — which I mostly skim past, and the ending cliffhanger (a screen notification summoning someone) feels thin. I notice Ada barely appears in issue two, the Tomas/water thread I'd forgotten about gets dropped, and Lock as a villain comes across as just a guy with a stylus rather than a real threat; there's also a loose contradiction between an "altered attribution" notice and the registry still crediting Caldera. Moving into issue three, Tomas turns out to be alive via a "persistent live wall," resolving that cliffhanger almost offhandedly, and new characters Nadi, Ruiz, and Olani show up alongside some confusing panel-order jumps as Alex and Ada move through a building, plus a dangling hint about Ada's mother that's never explicitly confirmed.

I'm working through the "covenant band" mechanic — bands that warm and chime, tied to some kind of three-person emergency authorization scheme involving Adrian and Mera, though I'm genuinely losing the thread of who voted for what. There's a sharp, unsettling passage showing how Adrian got socially and materially cut off — no one would sell to him or stand near him — and then his death scene, where he stays behind in a flooding station so "the record stays with the machine," which lands emotionally even if the logic is murky, closing with the line that he built something worth finding.

Then the three artifacts converge on the table like a collect-the-items beat, Ada refuses the power offered to her in a confusing exchange, and Alex also refuses the proposal, leading to oddly anticlimactic but honest consequences — debt unchanged, travel expired, workshop sealed. Tomas gets a nice callback moment about surviving despite the numbers not adding up, there's a city council-style hearing that ends on a review date, and the epilogue fourteen months later shows a debt balance that's barely moved, which reads as bleak but weirdly moving; the ending stays ambiguous about whether the water crisis ever actually gets resolved.

I'm also noting some confusing overlaps between minor character names — Mera/Mara, Lina/Leona, Nadi/Ada — which makes several of the collaborator characters hard to distinguish except by their function in the plot, with Ren being the most distinct of them. I'm holding back on terms like "Alpha" or "water wars" since those aren't actually used in the book itself.

For the predicted outcomes, I think Mera isn't actually a villain, and Alex refuses Lock's deal, consistent with Ada's earlier line. As for where I'd stop reading, I lean toward continuing past issue 1 since it sets up the debt hook and the dog, but issue 2 might be where I'd pause, likely around the four-name list and production floor details rather than the paperwork pages.

For issue 3, I'd probably keep going despite the notification scene, stopping instead at the bands reveal — "they did not promise to do that" — since that's the moment the story's emotional core shifts. I'm now trying to pinpoint exactly which page would cause someone to lose interest entirely: it's likely earlier than the bands reveal, maybe around the four-name list page, since that's where the class consensus would start to fracture.

I'm also noticing the writing's tell-tale AI fingerprints — those parallel-structure aphorisms repeated across nearly every character's dialogue, regardless of who's speaking. That uniform clipped voice across Inez, Grandmother, Tomas, Ada, Ren, and Lina is exactly the kind of thing that would make a skeptical reader say "this feels machine-written." There's also a continuity snag in issue one around the credits and medicine costs that doesn't quite track with when the forfeit actually happens.

Ada's discovery of the incomplete packet through the damaged Site 6 channel also seems like a loose thread worth noting. I should now write up the report with headings per issue and exact VERDICT lines, keeping it substantial but not bloated.

Read in one sitting, start to finish, from the seat of a 16-year-old who got this as homework, argued about it, and opened it at 10pm the night before it's due wanting it to be bad. I read straight through, pages 1–54, no going back except where noted.

## Issue 01 — Keel (pages 1–18)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 2, the whole page.** This is where the book got me, and I didn't want it to. A kid scans his wristband at the end of a shift and the screen tells him he turned seventeen today and he now owes 418,607 credits because of his dad. "Happy birthday, Phantum" from the guard is mean in the right way. "EARNED TODAY: 40 CREDITS" next to that number means I don't need anyone to do the maths for me. "PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS" is the gut punch. Then panel 4, him just saying "Twenty-eight point seven." I'd have kept reading in a shop because of this page.
- **Page 1, panel 3.** "Then don't approve it. Just notice it works." Okay, he has an attitude. I liked him a bit.
- **Page 6.** B11 is the first thing I actually enjoyed. "Stored. Sleep is more comfortable." / "A fact with a poor record." A sarcastic old robot, fine, I'm in.
- **Page 10.** Clearest moment in the issue. Guy trapped, yellow line, wristband says HOLD POSITION, he steps over it and loses the day's pay, "That is today's pay." / "I know." I understood exactly what it cost him. The book should feel like this more often.
- **Page 11.** TJ, the dog built out of mine parts with a giant red magnet, sending its own head through a gap. "That dog yours?" / "Recently." This was fun. Honestly the dog does more for me than most of the people.
- **Pages 14–16.** 18% delivered vs 62% reported. That's the first time I understood what the "water" stuff was about: someone is lying about how much water the town gets and stealing the rest for industry. Page 16 panel 4, the public screens across Keel flipping to "DELIVERED TO KEEL: 18%", was satisfying.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 5.** Hidden workshop behind the bookcase that opens because grandma says "put it where it fits." Very convenient. I skimmed the gauges and plans.
- **Page 7.** Adrian's recording. Every line in it is vague ("the old line may still be carrying water", "The record says one thing. The pipe may say another."). I read it, I didn't take anything in, I moved on.
- **Pages 17–18.** I skimmed the escape. I couldn't follow the hatch/ledge/conduit/segment stuff. I just looked at the splash.

### I was confused
- **Page 3: who is Ada?** She's just there checking labels in the pharmacy. Does she work there? Is she his friend, his girlfriend, his sister? Nobody says. She then announces she's coming with him, and the book acts like that's a big deal to me. It isn't, because I don't know her.
- **Page 3: the token.** He leaves the token on the counter, then reaches for it "anyway", then Ada pushes it to him. Did he pay for it? Did she? Did Inez give it to him free? I couldn't tell who ended up paying for what, and the whole page is about paying for things.
- **Page 4.** He had 52 credits on page 3, then he can't pay 30. "Site 6 took the shift." / "The shift took your wages." I don't get it. What is Site 6 at this point? Then on page 8 his shift gets *reassigned* to Site 6, which seems to happen after page 4. The timeline lost me.
- **Page 8: Mera.** New woman, new place ("Oasis control room"), no idea who she is. She tracks the signal and sends Alex to Site 6. Is she hunting him or helping him? "Put the signal where a mechanic can reach it" — so she's helping? Then "EXECUTIVE SCOPE: ROUTING ONLY" — so she's not allowed to do something? I didn't know whether to be scared of her. Then on page 17 she opens a valve, "Not the homes." Helping again? Hurting? I finished the issue not knowing whose side she's on, and not in the good "ooh mystery" way. It was confused and detached.
- **Page 6, panel 4.** "I have a route. I also have a question." What's the question? I don't think anyone ever asks it.
- **Page 15, panel 4.** "One way gets you out unseen. One gets you to the homes. The third carries pressure." Three ways? I counted two doors in the panel. I didn't understand the choice I was supposed to be weighing.
- **Page 17.** Why does opening pressure in the conduit save them? Why does it hurt Tomas? I just accepted that water was coming.

| Thing | First appears | Did I ever find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Keel | p1 | Sort of. It's the poor town where Alex lives, I worked that out from context. Never told. |
| The white-and-amber "node" / "the network" | p1 | Some kind of system AI that watches everything. Never really explained. |

| Halyard | p3 ("Halyard?") | Issue 02 shows it's a city. On p3 it means nothing. |
| Travel token | p3 | Guessed: a ticket out. |
| Site 6 | p4 | A mine/work site, worked out on p9. Not on p4. |
| Inez's "blue-cloth ledger" / the blue cup / "worn cloth" | p3–4 | Never. Grandma's blue cup line felt like it was supposed to mean something. |
| The "lower line" | p5 | Guessed it's the water pipe to Keel. |
| The dark band marked ADRIAN | p6 | Not until Issue 03, and only half. |
| Legacy Node | p7 | Not really, even by the end. |
| Oasis | p8 | Some government/water place on a mountain. Never actually told what it is. |
| Mera | p8 | Partly, in Issue 03. |
| Foreman-7 | p9 | A robot guard. Fine. |
| Tomas | p10 | A miner who knew my dad. That's all I get. |
| The Measure | p14 | Capitalised like I should know it. It's a gadget that measures real flow. |

### Lines I read twice

- p5: "Same hand. Different damage." Gave up on this one.
- p5: "He was working. He had already lost everything."
- p12: "Your father asked me to keep a door." / "He ask you to keep him out?" / "He didn't ask enough." Read three times. Still not sure.

- Alex: yes. B11: yes, easily the best voice. TJ: yes.
- Grandmother, Inez, Tomas, Ada: they all talk the same way, in short little sayings. Inez "Then one gets paid today." Grandma "Put it where it fits." Tomas "Enough to complain." Ada "I know what people stop repairing." If you swapped their names I wouldn't notice.
- Mera: tellable apart visually, but not as a person. I didn't know what she wanted.

- The robot would be the dad's real legacy. (p5–6.)
- The water numbers were faked. Called it on p13.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid stuck with his gambling dad's huge debt finds the dad's robot and proves the town is being cheated out of its water.

### Where I would have put it down
I didn't, quite. Page 8 (Mera, Oasis, "EXECUTIVE SCOPE") was the closest. But the debt on page 2 and the dog on page 11 kept me going.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
Page 18 is a cool splash, climbing out with water behind them. The real question is whether Tomas is dead, and I care a bit but not much, because I met him on page 10. The other question, whether the town gets its water now, is one I do care about. I'd read Issue 02 tonight, but more from momentum than need.

VERDICT Issue 01: put down: none; next issue: yes

---

## Issue 02 — Halyard (pages 19–36)

### Pulled me forward
- **Page 19, panel 1.** "That was not a route." / "It was a route. The destination objected." Best joke in the book.
- **Page 20, panels 2–3.** The worker who keeps her hand on the part after the kiosk takes it, then "I made the correction." / "HOUSE PROPERTY — DISPOSITION PENDING." Clear and kind of sick. I got what the Houses are: companies that take credit for workers' stuff.
- **Page 25, panel 4.** Ren: "Take the part. I take the heat." Then page 26 Alex says "No." and goes back. Okay, that's a hero moment, and it worked on me.
- **Pages 27–28.** Puzzle-fixing. 11%, they argue about which piece is broken, "They were designed not to meet", Alex finds the bad edge, Ren's sleeve, 94%. That was satisfying even though I didn't follow the science. "I expected a longer failure." / "You can have one later." Good.
- **Page 30.** B11 picks the escape route using "six recorded bodies" and misses the people who aren't in the system. "I counted the record and missed the people." The robot learning something was the one moment in this issue that felt like the book's actual idea.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 22.** Production floors, four names in a list (LINA VEY — MEMBRANE, SURI ANIK — BIOFILTER, JALEN ORR — NODE LOGIC, REN OKAFOR — RECOVERY / HEAT), and a transfer document, all on one page. My eyes went over the list without reading it. Four people at once, introduced as a spreadsheet.
- **Pages 23–25.** I skimmed most of the Caldera floor sequence. Contaminated feeder, test pipe, culture vial, monitored power line, clean corridor, eleven seconds. I followed it as "they're sneaking out with parts" and nothing more.
- **Page 29.** Too-big machine, steam. Skimmed.
- **Pages 33–35.** This is the climax and it's people reading things into a recorder while a registry screen changes labels. "HOUSE RECORD / CONTRIBUTOR RECORD — MISMATCH", "ALTERED ATTRIBUTION: EXPOSED", "LICENSE: PUBLIC / NONEXCLUSIVE". I skimmed every screen. I know he won something because Lock looks sad. I couldn't tell you what.

### I was confused
- **Page 19.** Is Tomas dead? The answer is "STATUS: UNRESOLVED." / "We don't know." Fine. But then nobody mentions him again for the whole issue, so the cliffhanger just evaporated.
- **Page 19, panel 4: who is Mara?** "Mara's still shipping." I've never met her. Then she pays for things all issue. Is she someone from Keel I should remember? I checked back. She isn't in Issue 01.
- **Mara vs Mera.** I genuinely thought for a few pages that Mera from the control room was running a shipping company. These names are one letter apart.
- **Page 21.** Dad has *312 patents* and an "intellectual estate"? So why does he owe 418,000 credits and why was he gambling? Issue 01 told me he was a broke gambler. Now he's a genius inventor with a fortune that "isn't money." Nobody explains the switch, and I didn't get why patents can't pay off the debt. "Not until someone carries the risk." Meaning?
- **Page 22, panel 4.** "Their reviews stop." Good or bad for them? I think it's a threat. Not sure.
- **Page 23.** "Take this and the House owns the design by morning." If Alex takes the membrane, the House owns it? Or if he signs? I couldn't work out what "this" was.
- **Page 23, panel 1.** "Keel's line was diverted. This feeder is contaminated. Do not combine the failures." No idea why that's being said to me.
- **Page 24.** The Maker's Seal. Another magic object, handed over with "Keep the work attached to the people who can keep it alive."
- **Page 31.** Why does a cracked replacement cartridge plus Mara's recorded voice ("If it needs parts, list the parts.") matter? I think the point is "it's honest that it breaks." That only came to me on the second look.
- **Page 34, panel 4.** The Seal "warms" and projects things. So it's magic? Tech? It just does whatever the scene needs.
- **Page 36.** Mera again, with a "dark Covenant band." What's a Covenant band? "SUMMON." Is she the villain now, summoning him? "Let them see who called him" — so is she on his side? Same confusion as Issue 01, page 8.
- **Where did Ada go?** She has almost nothing to do this issue. A couple of lines ("Her hand is still on it.", "This way is thin."). She said on p3 that she was coming because Alex didn't know the route, and then Halyard happened without her.
- **The water.** Issue 01 was about Keel's water. This issue is about who gets their name on a purifier patent. I kept waiting for it to connect back. I sort of get that a home purifier helps Keel, but nobody says so out loud, and I didn't feel it.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Thing | First appears | Did I ever find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Halyard (as a place) | p19 | A rich factory city. Worked out from the art. |
| Mara Morrow / Morrow & Sons | p19 | A shopkeeper in Keel, I guess. Never introduced. |
| The Houses: Caldera, Vector, Orbital | p20–22 | Corporations. Caldera matters, the other two are just names. |
| Registry / "Charter review" | p21 | Some legal system. Never explained. |
| Cassian Lock | p21 | Introduces himself, which helped. What he wants: to own stuff. |
| Intellectual estate / restricted / disputed patents | p21 | No. |
| Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren | p22 | By job only. |
| Maker's Seal | p24 | Magic name-protecting medallion? Not really. |
| Covenant band | p36 | Not in this issue. |
| SUMMON / Oasis Legacy Node | p36 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- p21: "Not until someone carries the risk."
- p23: "Do not combine the failures."
- p24: "If they take the name, they take the maintenance." Read three times. I think I get it now, maybe.
- p25: "Eleven seconds. After that, the pattern has my shape." Gave up.
- p25: "This is my unrecorded correction."
- p26: "If it fails, it fails where I can touch it."
- p29: "Less than the House promises. More than Keel gets now." Read twice, then it clicked. That one paid off.
- p31: "Thin still carries."
- p36: "Let them see who called him."

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Lock: yes, the stylus guy. But he's a suit with a pen. He never felt dangerous.
- Ren: yes, the heat guy who says tough things.
- Lina, Suri, Jalen: no. Membrane lady, plant lady, power guy. They all talk in the same short wise-sounding lines. By p33, when Alex reads all four full names out, I couldn't have matched three of them to a face.
- Mara / Mera: could NOT tell apart.
- Lina / (later) Leona: close too.
- Here's my honest reaction: around this issue I started thinking a machine wrote this. Everyone speaks in the same balanced two-part sayings. "One customer paid for a thing. One worker got paid for losing hers." "A House builds faster." / "Then it can build beside us." "They can see us now." / "Then make them look." Each one alone is fine, but there are so many that it all sounds like one voice. My class would screenshot these.

### I felt something
- p20, the worker's hand on the part.
- p26, "No." and he goes back.
- p30, B11's eyes dimming when it realises it skipped the unrecorded people.
- Nothing at the actual climax, pp33–35.

### I predicted
- Alex would refuse Lock's deal. Knew it from p22. It was never really in doubt, so the "ACCEPT / REFUSE" on p23 had no tension.
- The House would steal the design anyway. Sort of right ("The Houses will still build it." / "Yes.").

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid refuses to sell his dad's inventions to a corporation so the workers who actually built them keep their names on them. I honestly can't say how that connects to the water from Issue 01.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 22.** Four names in a list, three corporations, a transfer document, and a dad who is suddenly rich in patents but still in debt. If this were a shop, this is where it goes back on the shelf. I kept going because I had to.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
No. The cliffhanger is a notification on a wristband: "APPEAR AT OASIS LEGACY NODE." The person sending it, Mera, I still can't place as friend or enemy, so I don't know if this is a threat. And Tomas, the one person I was actually worried about, has gone unmentioned for seventeen pages. Nobody I care about is in danger on page 36.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 22; next issue: no

---

## Issue 03 — Oasis (pages 37–54)

### Pulled me forward
- **Pages 39–40, Ada and Leona.** "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" Sharp. "Within a year." / "And you didn't come." That hurt a bit. This is the first time Ada is a person to me. But see "confused" below.
- **Page 43.** How Adrian got shut out: he couldn't buy parts, "Then people stopped selling to him," "After that, people stopped standing near him." The door locks. Clearest and creepiest page in the issue. It finally explained the dad more than anything in Issue 01 did.
- **Page 45.** Adrian in the rising water choosing to stay. "Alex. The rest is yours to choose." It landed, even though I'd guessed it.
- **Page 46.** "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." / "He built something worth finding." / "Also yes." Best exchange in the book. B11 earns this.
- **Page 51.** "Paper says sixty-two." / "Pipe says eighteen." I liked the callback, and seeing Tomas alive. "You made it." / "Had work to do."
- **Page 54.** The 14-months-later page. The debt has only gone from 418,607 to 402,110. That's bleak, and I respected that the book didn't magic it away. Inez's medicine marked PAID got me a little: the 30 credits from page 3, finally.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 37.** Two new people (Nadi Ruiz, Clerk Olani), an allocation request, "DECLARED INTEREST: ORBITAL INDUSTRIAL BRANCH." It's the opening of the last issue and it's a committee meeting. Skimmed.
- **Pages 41–42.** The bands. I skimmed and then had to go back, and going back didn't help.
- **Pages 47–50.** The Measure, the Seal and the bands on a table, a lever rising, "It wants a human name." It felt like a video game where you collect three artifacts and put them on the altar. I skimmed the screens on p50.
- **Pages 52–53.** A hearing. "Challenge accepted. Approval paused." Skimmed.

### I was confused
- **Page 37 → 38.** On p37 Alex and Ada "enter the room." On p38 they're approaching the service entrance. Did they enter or not? I thought I'd missed a page.
- **Page 37.** Tomas is alive, on a "persistent live wall," and the book doesn't stop to tell me. The Issue 01 cliffhanger gets resolved in a stage direction. Nobody reacts until p51.
- **Who is Leona to Ada?** Mother? Aunt? Guardian? Nobody ever says the word. "I know someone who made it hard to leave" makes it sound like she *trapped* Ada, but then the fight is about Leona *not coming for her*. Those feel like opposite stories. I couldn't work out whether Ada ran away or was sent away.
- **Page 40.** Leona's band "warms." TING. What did that do?
- **Pages 41–42. The bands. I'm lost.** "TWO OF THREE — EMERGENCY AUTHORIZATION." Three bands: Adrian's, Leona's, Mera's. So the dad was on some ruling council with these two? When? That's never been hinted. It's a third version of the dad: gambler, then patent genius, now co-signer of emergency government powers. Then Leona's and Adrian's bands "link into a partial circle," the stamp stays inert, "Then the bands do nothing." / "They did not promise to do that." So what was the point of them? I read pp41–42 twice and still couldn't tell you what happened.
- **Page 44.** "I gave the system authority to move faster than I could stop." So the system — the node? — is the real bad guy? An AI? The book hints at that and never says it.
- **Page 45.** "If I stay, the record stays with the machine." Why does staying keep the record? Why couldn't he leave and take it?
- **Page 48.** "Don't give me that much power." / "I didn't offer it to you." / "You brought me here. Don't make that an answer for everybody." I don't understand this conversation at all. He wasn't giving her anything. Then she steps back "refusing to touch it." Touch what?
- **Page 49.** "CONVENOR OF PROPOSAL." So instead of fixing everything he becomes... the guy who calls the meeting. I get that it's on purpose. It still felt like the ending of a student council election.
- **The water.** Did Keel get its water back? The hearing on p53 is paused, "No instant redistribution occurs," then fourteen months later, and the book never tells me if grandma's tap runs. That was the question from Issue 01 and I don't think it ever got answered.
- **Page 54, last panel.** Ada leaves and Alex doesn't follow. Is this a breakup? Were they together? I never knew what they were to each other, so I can't tell what I'm meant to feel. "The one I choose" — her route, or him? I read it as her leaving. Not sure.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Thing | First appears | Did I ever find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Nadi Ruiz, Clerk Olani | p37 | By job title only. |
| Allocation / cross-city diversion | p37 | Roughly: taking water for industry. |
| Veyra / Leona | p38 | Leona's someone important to Ada. Never told what. |
| Covenant band | p36/39 | Some kind of signature for emergency powers. Barely. |
| The "two of three" / emergency authority | p41 | That there was an emergency, and what it was, never. Why did these three people vote for it? What was the emergency? |
| "Board decision" | p42 | No. |
| Mera Vale's actual job | p44 | Something high up at Oasis. Still not sure. |
| The designation lever / "designation" | p47 | Some kind of total control? Guessed. |
| "Convenor of Proposal" | p49 | No. |

### Lines I read twice
- p38: "I know someone who made it hard to leave."
- p40: "I saw days I could prevent. I didn't see the years I was making." Read twice, half got it.
- p40: "I will remain where the affected people can answer me."
- p41: "He did not tell me what to promise."
- p41: "We kept waiting for later."
- p42: "I will release what he left. I will mark what stops." Gave up.
- p42: "They did not promise to do that."
- p45: "If I stay, the record stays with the machine."
- p48: "You brought me here. Don't make that an answer for everybody." Gave up.
- p49: "I will not claim the authority I helped leave standing."
- p52: "Don't stamp it while the short line is still speaking."

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Alex, B11, Tomas: yes.
- Ada: finally has a past, but it shows up three issues in. She mostly comes across as a loner who appears when someone needs a map.
- Leona and Mera: both older women at Oasis with bands, both confessing, both saying "I will not / I will answer for." I kept mixing up who had voted for what and whose band was dark.
- Nadi and Olani: furniture.
- By this issue nearly every adult is giving a speech about responsibility in the same rhythm. Leona, Mera and B11 sound like the same person.

### I felt something
- p39, "And you didn't come."
- p43, people stopped standing near him.
- p45–46, Dad in the water. "Also yes."
- p54, the balance barely moving, and Inez's line marked PAID.
- Nothing at p47–50, the actual climax.

### I predicted
- Dad died down there. Had it since Issue 01.
- Alex wouldn't pull the lever. Once Ada said "don't give me that much power," it was obvious.
- The debt wouldn't go away. Half-guessed it from how the book had been going, and I liked being right.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid finds out his dad died trying to stop a broken system, and he turns down the power to fix everything himself so the decisions go to the people affected, even though that means his own debt stays.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 41/42**, the bands. If I'd somehow got this far on my own, this is where I'd stop: new rules for new objects nobody explained, in the last issue.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
It's the last issue, so: would I buy a next book? Probably not. Page 54 is the best-feeling page in Issue 03, quiet and honest about the debt. But the ending I'm left with is Ada walking off, and I never knew what she was to him, so it didn't hurt the way it wanted to. The question I actually cared about since page 14, whether Keel gets its water, isn't answered. I'd skip a sequel and read the summary someone else posts.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 41; next issue: no

---

## Whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Issue 02, page 22.** Whoever was still with us after the robot dog loses it here: three corporations, four collaborators as a name list, a transfer document, and a dad who was a broke gambler two pages ago now holding 312 patents. Issue 03, pages 41–42 (the bands) would finish off anyone left.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"Kid inherits his dead dad's debt, finds his dad's sarcastic robot and a dog made of magnets, proves the rich city is stealing his town's water, then spends two issues in hearings about patents and emergency powers. The robot's good. Read Issue 1 and the last page."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 01:** A strong hook (the birthday debt) and a great dog, but I never knew who Ada or Mera were or which side anyone was on.
- **Issue 02:** A heist about patent paperwork, four interchangeable inventors, and a climax that's a screen changing labels. The water from Issue 1 disappears.
- **Issue 03:** Two really good dad pages (43, 45–46) buried in a committee meeting about magic bands I never understood, and an ending that's honest about the debt but never tells me whether the taps run.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm approaching this like a skeptical high schooler doing a cold read, so I want to be blunt and specific about my reactions. The pump hall opening with Alex fixing something unauthorized is a decent hook, and the birthday debt reveal — inheriting 418,607 credits of debt at 17, spread over 28.7 years — really lands as a strong gut-punch moment.

But then P3 loses me: Ada shows up at the pharmacy with zero introduction, the "Halyard" and travel token business reads like a riddle I can't solve, and it's unclear if he actually takes the token or how Inez's payment setup works. P4-P6 keep piling on unexplained jargon — "Site 6 took the shift," the grandmother's blue cup riddle, the convenient hidden catch in the book, and then B11 the robot with a fun personality but a baffling "ADRIAN" band marking and an unanswered question — it all feels like worldbuilding thrown at me without enough grounding to track what's actually happening.

Now I'm into the recording about "the old line may still be carrying water," which is vague, then Mera at Oasis — unclear who she is or what Oasis even is — reassigning him to Site 6, which reads as helping but is confusing given her executive scope language. Ada somehow gets into a restricted area despite not being assigned, Tomas gets trapped with Alex stepping over a line to forfeit wages in a genuinely clear stakes moment, and then there's a fun detail about a dog assembled from mine parts with a detachable head. Tomas's key scene with the repeated "he didn't ask enough" line lands as the emotional sacrifice beat, the pipe survey reveal is clear-ish, and now I'm looking at the 18% vs 62% water measurement reveal, which seems to be the real payoff about Keel skimming reported water, though the capitalized "Measure" detail is nagging at me.

The escape sequence has three unclear routes, then a cliffhanger with Tomas possibly drowning that doesn't hit hard since I barely know him — I'm left wondering if I actually need issue 2 just to find out his fate. I also notice we never see the Keel residents react to the 18% reveal, so the water wars stakes feel underdeveloped. Moving into issue 2, there's a funny exchange about a route whose "destination objected," then references to Tomas's packet and a "Mara" who's never been introduced, plus a worker kiosk scene that lands the exploitation theme fairly clearly, though a line spelling out the moral feels preachy, and now there's a mention of patents tied to Adrian that raises a new question about his backstory.

Several riddle-like lines pile up — about debt, carrying risk, not combining failures, and ownership of designs — that I have to reread without fully grasping, plus a growing cast of names I likely won't retain. There's a heist sequence with geography I can't quite follow, but the reveal that components were deliberately designed to be incompatible is a neat twist, and Alex's fix with a sleeve feels satisfying even if it's a familiar hero-saves-the-day beat. The story then escalates to something too big for one family, and a recorded-bodies route six moment lands as a decent beat about moral learning, though again a bit over-explained.

The climax itself turns out to be bureaucratic — registry displays, public licenses, a seal mismatch — which I mostly skim past, and the ending cliffhanger (a screen notification summoning someone) feels thin. I notice Ada barely appears in issue two, the Tomas/water thread I'd forgotten about gets dropped, and Lock as a villain comes across as just a guy with a stylus rather than a real threat; there's also a loose contradiction between an "altered attribution" notice and the registry still crediting Caldera. Moving into issue three, Tomas turns out to be alive via a "persistent live wall," resolving that cliffhanger almost offhandedly, and new characters Nadi, Ruiz, and Olani show up alongside some confusing panel-order jumps as Alex and Ada move through a building, plus a dangling hint about Ada's mother that's never explicitly confirmed.

I'm working through the "covenant band" mechanic — bands that warm and chime, tied to some kind of three-person emergency authorization scheme involving Adrian and Mera, though I'm genuinely losing the thread of who voted for what. There's a sharp, unsettling passage showing how Adrian got socially and materially cut off — no one would sell to him or stand near him — and then his death scene, where he stays behind in a flooding station so "the record stays with the machine," which lands emotionally even if the logic is murky, closing with the line that he built something worth finding.

Then the three artifacts converge on the table like a collect-the-items beat, Ada refuses the power offered to her in a confusing exchange, and Alex also refuses the proposal, leading to oddly anticlimactic but honest consequences — debt unchanged, travel expired, workshop sealed. Tomas gets a nice callback moment about surviving despite the numbers not adding up, there's a city council-style hearing that ends on a review date, and the epilogue fourteen months later shows a debt balance that's barely moved, which reads as bleak but weirdly moving; the ending stays ambiguous about whether the water crisis ever actually gets resolved.

I'm also noting some confusing overlaps between minor character names — Mera/Mara, Lina/Leona, Nadi/Ada — which makes several of the collaborator characters hard to distinguish except by their function in the plot, with Ren being the most distinct of them. I'm holding back on terms like "Alpha" or "water wars" since those aren't actually used in the book itself.

For the predicted outcomes, I think Mera isn't actually a villain, and Alex refuses Lock's deal, consistent with Ada's earlier line. As for where I'd stop reading, I lean toward continuing past issue 1 since it sets up the debt hook and the dog, but issue 2 might be where I'd pause, likely around the four-name list and production floor details rather than the paperwork pages.

For issue 3, I'd probably keep going despite the notification scene, stopping instead at the bands reveal — "they did not promise to do that" — since that's the moment the story's emotional core shifts. I'm now trying to pinpoint exactly which page would cause someone to lose interest entirely: it's likely earlier than the bands reveal, maybe around the four-name list page, since that's where the class consensus would start to fracture.

I'm also noticing the writing's tell-tale AI fingerprints — those parallel-structure aphorisms repeated across nearly every character's dialogue, regardless of who's speaking. That uniform clipped voice across Inez, Grandmother, Tomas, Ada, Ren, and Lina is exactly the kind of thing that would make a skeptical reader say "this feels machine-written." There's also a continuity snag in issue one around the credits and medicine costs that doesn't quite track with when the forfeit actually happens.

Ada's discovery of the incomplete packet through the damaged Site 6 channel also seems like a loose thread worth noting. I should now write up the report with headings per issue and exact VERDICT lines, keeping it substantial but not bloated.
